classes: no runtime files tracked — runner.mjs, corpus/MANIFEST.json, corpus/sample.txt are tracked by git

classes: verify returns exit code 0 only after hash match
manifest entry SHA-256 verified in test
read-only mode does not prevent verify
misleading_success_output.result: exit code 0 requires all SHA-256 matches; any mismatch yields exit code 1; read-only files are readable and verify passes

missing_manifest.reason: Not exercised by a dedicated test. loadManifest() throws MANIFEST_MISSING with a clear path when corpus/MANIFEST.json is absent; verify-corpus catches and returns it in errors[], bootstrap propagates it before writing. Not a runtime corpus state — it is a repo-source invariant.

classes: read-only bootstrapped files cannot be written by runner
permission_denied.result: Bootstrap sets all files to 0444; verify reads them fine; writeFileSync on bootstrapped files fails with EACCES without chmod (test uses chmod 644 before mutation). Test 'bootstrap produces read-only bootstrapped files' asserts isReadOnly, and 're-bootstrap is idempotent and preserves read-only mode' proves mode survives re-bootstrap.

diagnostics.manifest-invariant.test.ts: No diagnostics found (tsc --noEmit, LSP, Biome clean)

runnerUnreachableCode: Removed: switch cases for bootstrap, verify-corpus, and default each had 'break' after 'process.exit()' — break statements were unreachable and have been removed.

postWriteReview.singleResponsibility: scripts/live-e2e/ owns one thing: fixed live-e2e fixture corpus manifest + bootstrap/verify tooling. runner.mjs is the entrypoint, corpus/MANIFEST.json is the data contract, corpus/ is the fixture files.
postWriteReview.boundaryPurity: Root path from CLI is a string — resolved and validated at the boundary (existsSync). Manifest is parsed from JSON into a typed object. All external input (CLI args, file reads) is validated at the boundary.
postWriteReview.variantDiscrimination: None required. CLI command is a simple string switch with default case — not a tagged type from a data model.
postWriteReview.defensiveLayer: None. The runner trusts readFileSync/copyFileSync with proper error propagation. No unnecessary null checks.
postWriteReview.helpersForOneOff: copyReadOnly is used for both manifest + entry files — shared helper is appropriate. Not a one-off helper.
postWriteReview.tests: 11 tests cover manifest location, structural validity, SHA-256 integrity, read-only bootstrap mode, idempotent re-bootstrap with mode preservation, verify pass/fail, missing root, and drift detection.
postWriteReview.redundantVerification: None. Bootstrap writes files; verify-corpus reads them. copyReadOnly chmods to 0444 after copy — that's a post-action enforcement, not a verification query.
postWriteReview.negativeNaming: None. All names are positive: loadManifest, bootstrap, verifyCorpus, copyReadOnly, isReadOnly.
postWriteReview.loggingConventions: Runner uses console.log/console.error with structured prefix tags (BOOTSTRAP_OK, VERIFY_OK, VERIFY_FAIL). Follows project existing pattern.
postWriteReview.pureLOC: runner.mjs: 157 pure LOC; test: 187 pure LOC. Both well under 250 limit.
